html:
The Constitution of Kuwait was adopted in November 1962, a year after independence. It set up the National Assembly, first elected in 1963, the oldest and strongest elected parliament among the Gulf monarchies.

The emir keeps great power and names the government, but the assembly passes laws and the budget and can question ministers and vote no confidence in them. That reflects Kuwait's old bargain between the ruling family and the merchant families.

The emir suspended the assembly in 1976 and again in 1986, and restored it after the Gulf War. Clashes between assembly and cabinet have often stalled government. Women won the right to vote in 2005. In 2024 the emir suspended parts of the constitution once more.
